# 6.2 - The Multiplication Rule {.unnumbered}

You guess on 3 multiple-choice questions. Each question has 4 choices. What is the probability you get all 3 right?

Each guess has a $\frac{1}{4}$ chance. The questions do not affect each other, so you multiply:

$$
P(\text{all 3 right}) = \frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{1}{4} \cdot \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{64}
$$

That is about a 1.6% chance. In this lesson, you learn when and how to multiply probabilities.

:::{.objectives}
- [ ] I decide if two events are independent or dependent.
- [ ] I use the multiplication rule for independent events.
- [ ] I use the general multiplication rule for dependent events.
- [ ] I use the complement for "at least one" questions.
:::

### 6.2.1 - Independent Events

Two events are {{< glink "independent events" text="independent" >}} if one happening does not change the probability of the other.

:::{.remember title="Independent Events"}
$$
P(A \cap B) = P(A) \cdot P(B)
$$
:::

**Example:** Flip a coin and roll a number cube.

$$
P(\text{heads} \cap 6) = \frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{6} = \frac{1}{12}
$$

***

### 6.2.2 - Dependent Events

Two events are {{< glink "dependent events" text="dependent" >}} if one happening changes the probability of the other.

A bag has 5 red and 3 blue marbles. Draw 2 marbles.

| **{{< glink "with replacement" text="With replacement" >}}** (put the first one back) | **{{< glink "without replacement" text="Without replacement" >}}** (keep the first one out) |
|---|---|
| The second draw is the same as the first. Independent. | The bag changes: 4 red and 3 blue are left. Dependent. |
| $P(\text{red, red}) = \frac{5}{8} \cdot \frac{5}{8} = \frac{25}{64}$ | $P(\text{red, red}) = \frac{5}{8} \cdot \frac{4}{7} = \frac{20}{56} = \frac{5}{14}$ |

:::{.remember title="The General Multiplication Rule"}
$$
P(A \cap B) = P(A) \cdot P(B \mid A)
$$

$P(B \mid A)$ is read "the probability of $B$ **given** $A$." It is the probability of $B$ after $A$ has already happened. The bar $\mid$ means "given."
:::

In the marble example, $P(\text{red second} \mid \text{red first}) = \frac{4}{7}$.

***

### 6.2.3 - "At Least One"

"At least one" questions are often easier with the {{< glink complement >}}:

$$
P(\text{at least one wrong}) = 1 - P(\text{all right})
$$

:::{.you-try title="You guess on 3 questions with 4 choices each. Find $P(\text{at least one wrong})$."}
$P(\text{all right}) = \frac{1}{64}$, so $P(\text{at least one wrong}) = 1 - \frac{1}{64} = \frac{63}{64}$.
:::

{{< practice >}}

Work with a partner. Compare answers when you finish each problem.

**Independent Events**

1. These events are independent. Find each probability.

   a. Flip a coin 3 times. $P(\text{3 heads})$

   b. Roll a number cube twice. $P(\text{two 6s})$

   c. A basketball player makes 80% of her free throws. $P(\text{she makes 2 in a row})$

   d. Same player. $P(\text{she misses both})$

2. You guess on a 5-question true-or-false quiz.

   a. $P(\text{all 5 right})$

   b. $P(\text{at least one wrong})$

***

**Dependent Events**

3. A bag has 4 green and 6 yellow marbles. Draw 2 marbles.

   a. Find $P(\text{green, green})$ **with** replacement.

   b. Find $P(\text{green, green})$ **without** replacement.

   c. Why is the answer to (b) smaller?

4. Independent or dependent? Explain.

   a. Flip a coin, then roll a number cube.

   b. Pick a class president, then pick a vice president from the students who are left.

   c. Draw a card, put it back, shuffle, and draw again.

   d. It rains today, and you carry an umbrella today.

5. At a school, $P(\text{late}) = 0.2$ and $P(\text{detention} \mid \text{late}) = 0.5$.

   a. Find $P(\text{late} \cap \text{detention})$.

   b. Explain what your answer means in words.
